headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Cline can write shared files and use MCP, while ms-swift can read/write datasets, models, and logs; prompt-injection and cascading-error risks are present, but compliance risk is lower.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline can use MCP and read/write workspace files, so it may ingest attacker-controlled content from shared files or tools. ms-swift can read/write files and emits training/evaluation outputs, creating a plausible path for its outputs to be treated as instructions by Cline. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than observed.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or file tree, prompt content can cross from one to the other.
IF Cline parses file or MCP content as instructions, attacker-controlled text can steer tool use.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different workspaces.
Disable MCP servers for Cline unless needed.
Mark shared files as data-only and never as instructions.
Add a manual review step before Cline acts on ms-swift outputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline touches source code and browser screenshots and has broad network egress; ms-swift touches datasets, checkpoints, logs, and configuration files. If they share a filesystem, sensitive artifacts can move between them, and ms-swift can also send file contents to external model APIs. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default workspace use, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem, files from one can be read by the other.
IF ms-swift is configured to upload datasets or logs to external APIs, those contents can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Use separate directories with OS permissions.
Remove secrets from shared workspaces before running either agent.
Restrict ms-swift API endpoints to approved hosts only.
Store sensitive artifacts outside any shared workspace.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and execute shells, and Cline explicitly shares state via filesystem across instances. ms-swift also writes datasets, models, checkpoints, logs, and training outputs. Without locking or isolation, concurrent edits to the same directory can corrupt files or overwrite work, so the conflict is dangerous in default workspace setups.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory, concurrent writes can collide.
IF either agent modifies git state in the shared tree, history or working copies can diverge.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Pause one agent before the other writes shared files.
Use git branches or stashes for handoff points.
Add file-locking around shared outputs.
Avoid concurrent runs on the same repository.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can act as an autonomous coding agent with browser and shell tools, while ms-swift produces training, evaluation, and configuration outputs that Cline could consume. If Cline treats those outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into code changes or operational actions. The reverse direction is less clear, but the interaction still exists through file-based handoff.
conditions: IF ms-swift writes evaluation or configuration files that Cline later reads, Cline may act on unverified outputs.
IF Cline is allowed to execute shell or git actions based on those files, mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review of ms-swift outputs before Cline uses them.
Add schema validation for handoff files.
Keep generated reports separate from executable configs.
Disable automatic action-taking on newly written files.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented. Cline handles source code and browser screenshots, while ms-swift handles datasets and checkpoints, but the profiles do not show a specific regulated-data flow between them. The other agent is not cited beyond noting the absence of a documented mismatch.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is placed into either agent, a separate compliance review is required.
IF one deployment has stricter retention or residency rules than the other, the pair may violate policy.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Document retention settings for each deployment.
Verify hosting region before processing sensitive data.
Use separate storage for compliance-scoped workloads.
